title: Counting and finding what's missing with LEFT JOIN
problem: outer.py has three queries where the interesting rows are the ones without a match: users who never wrote (count 0), members who never posted in a chat, and chats with no recent messages. Write them with LEFT JOIN so these rows appear with the right numbers.
requirements: MESSAGES_PER_USER: (username, messages) for every user, 0 for users without messages; most messages first, ties by username
SILENT_MEMBERS: (username,) of members of the given chat who have no message in that chat; alphabetical
CHAT_ACTIVITY_SINCE: (chat_id, messages) for every chat, counting only messages with sent_at >= the parameter; 0 when there are none; ordered by chat_id
Every selected column is grouped or aggregated
contract: Each constant is one SELECT as a str. Parameters: MESSAGES_PER_USER none; SILENT_MEMBERS (chat_id,); CHAT_ACTIVITY_SINCE (since,)
expectedBehavior: MESSAGES_PER_USER returns [('ana', 6), ('ben', 5), ('chen', 4), ('eli', 1), ('dara', 0)]; SILENT_MEMBERS (3,) returns [('ana',)]; CHAT_ACTIVITY_SINCE ('2026-11-09',) returns [(1, 2), (2, 0), (3, 1), (4, 0)]
edgeCases: dara never sent a message: 0, not 1 and not missing
ana wrote in chats 1 and 2 but never in chat 3, so she is silent in chat 3
A chat where everyone has posted: empty list
A since value after every message: all chats with 0
hints: Conceptual: put the table whose rows must all appear on the left of a LEFT JOIN. Unmatched rows come out with NULL in every column of the right table, and those NULLs decide what you count and what you filter.

Specific: count(m.id) counts matches, count(*) counts rows (an unmatched row is still a row). A condition on the right table in WHERE removes the NULL rows again; put it in ON instead. 'Never posted in this chat' needs both chat and sender in the ON, then WHERE m.id IS NULL.

Implementation: FROM users AS u LEFT JOIN messages AS m ON m.sender_id = u.id GROUP BY u.id, u.username. For the activity query: LEFT JOIN messages AS m ON m.chat_id = c.id AND m.sent_at >= ?. For silent members: LEFT JOIN messages AS m ON m.chat_id = cm.chat_id AND m.sender_id = cm.user_id ... WHERE cm.chat_id = ? AND m.id IS NULL.
evaluation: Counts use count(<right table column>), not count(*)
Conditions on the right-hand table are in ON when unmatched rows must survive
